newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel to advise cut in FILP in 1998/99 - Jiji.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel to advise cut in FILP in 1998/99 - Jiji.

text.p: A Japanese government advisory panel will submit proposals later on Wednesday to reform the fiscal investment and loans programme (FILP), including one that would cut spending in the programme for the fiscal year starting next April, Jiji news agency said.
The move would follow spending cuts in the programme in the 1997/98 fiscal year, the first in 12 years, Jiji said.

The proposals, to be submitted to the Finance Ministry and the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications (MPT), will also say that no new loans should be made to financially troubled Japan National Railway Settlement Corp. They will also allow borrowers from the programme to issue bonds without guarantees from the government, Jiji said.
The advisory panel is scheduled to meet this afternoon.
FILP, dubbed Japan's second national budget, uses deposits from the MPT and the Welfare Ministry to fund government-affiliated financial institutions and other quasi-government bodies.
